newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile says Brazil import rules may violate accord.
newsitem.headline: Chile says Brazil import rules may violate accord.

text.p: New Brazilian rules to restrict import financing could break an agreement signed last year between Chile and the four-nation Mercosur trade bloc, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said on Monday.
"We have expressed our unhappiness with these measures to the Brazilian government," Insulza told reporters.
"It seems to us a negative change in Brazil's policy of opening up its trade."
When Chile signed the accord with the Mercosur bloc, which links Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay, all sides agreed not to adopt measures that would in practice increase tariffs, he said.

"We understand that this is a measure parallel to tariffs by a country in the Mercosur which hurts trade with Chile, and this may be in violation of the treaty we signed with the Mercosur," Insulza said.
The new rules have already brought howls of protest from Argentine industry and government.
Insulza said Chile believed it would be easier to resolve the dispute by relying on the Mercosur's own regulations, instead of turning to the World Trade Organization (WTO).
"If we went to the WTO, our mechanisms for solving controversies would probably not be greater to those which we have with Mercosur...Probably they would be longer and more cumbersome," he said.
Chile's ambassador in Brazil, Heraldo Munoz, is working in parallel with representatives of Mercosur bloc members to look for a solution to the dispute over imports, Insulza said.
